sources.titre: platform: SAML IdP-initiated flow and metadata upload

tours.texte: we have SP-initiated saml working behind saml_sso. now add IdP-initiated: POST /auth/saml/acs without a prior AuthnRequest, validate InResponseTo absent, relay state = workspace slug. also an endpoint for admins to upload idp metadata xml. look at auth/saml/ first

I'll start by reading the existing SAML module.

Reading auth/saml/service.py, auth/saml/routes.py and tests/auth/test_saml_sp.py…

Current state:
- `build_authn_request()` stores the request ID in Redis for 5 minutes
- `/auth/saml/acs` rejects any response whose InResponseTo is not in Redis
- signature algorithm checked against SAML_MIN_SIG_ALG (rsa-sha256)

Plan for IdP-initiated:
1. Accept responses with no InResponseTo only if the workspace has `allow_idp_initiated=true`
2. Read the workspace from RelayState (slug), fall back to the Issuer → workspace mapping
3. Keep a short replay cache on the assertion ID (10 min) since there is no request ID to match
4. New endpoint POST /admin/sso/metadata (multipart), admin role only, parses entityID, SSO URL and signing cert

Shall I go ahead?
go

- auth/saml/service.py: `handle_idp_initiated()`, replay cache on assertion ID

Alert: consumer group ingest-events lag > 500,000 messages on partitions 0–11.
First seen: 2026-11-12 09:14 UTC · Environment: production · Service: ingest-worker
Events: 212
Last error: runtime: out of memory: cannot allocate 10485760-byte block
Stack: ingest/worker/batch.go:118 (*Batcher).flush
🔴 SEV2 declared: ingest lag climbing, events since ~08:50 UTC are not showing up in customer dashboards. IC: Noa. Comms: Rachel.
First guess: Kafka broker disk? broker-2 was at 81% yesterday.

Not the brokers, disk is at 62%. The ingest-worker pods are OOM-looping since the v2.14.0 deploy at 08:47. v2.14.0 raised the default max_batch_bytes from 1 MB to 10 MB (ingest#412) and the pods have a 512 Mi memory limit.
Rolling back ingest to v2.13.3.
Rollback done, consumers stable, lag draining.
Status page updated. Tickets so far from Orbitly and Zest Grocers.
Lag back to zero at 12:27. Dashboards were up to ~3h40 behind at the peak. Looks like no data loss, Lior is verifying the counts.
Reconciliation done: event counts per workspace match the Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC. Nothing lost, just late.

Authors: Lior Ben-David, Noa Friedman · Status: final · Severity: SEV2

Summary
On Thursday Nov 12, between 08:47 and 12:27 UTC (3h40), customer dashboards showed stale data. Events kept arriving in Kafka and were processed late by the ingestion pipeline; no event was lost (reconciliation of Nov 13).

Root cause
ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default max_batch_bytes from 1 MB to 10 MB to improve throughput. With the 512 Mi memory limit, the ingest-worker pods ran out of memory on the first large batch and crash-looped. The change went to all pods at once.

Detection
We had no alert on consumer lag. The first signal was a Sentry out-of-memory alert at 09:14, 27 minutes after the deploy. An early hypothesis (Kafka broker disk) was ruled out at 09:41.

Resolution
Rollback to v2.13.3 at 10:05; lag fully drained at 12:27. ingest#419 reverted the default and added a memory guard (merged Nov 13).

Impact
All workspaces had delayed dashboards. 4 customers contacted support (Orbitly, Zest Grocers, 2 trial accounts). Maya sent an incident report to Orbitly and Zest Grocers on Nov 15.

Action items
1. KES-431 – Page the on-call when consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes (owner: Noa, due Nov 20)
2. KES-432 – Ingest config changes go to the canary pool first (owner: Daniel, due Nov 27)
3. KES-433 – Raise worker memory limit to 1 Gi and add a load test on batch sizes (owner: Lior, due Nov 27)

What went well: rollback took 13 minutes once the cause was found.

a customer is claiming an SLA credit after a 3h40 dashboard delay. what are typical service credit terms for a b2b saas with a 99.9% uptime SLA? how would a 3h40 outage count

Service credits in B2B SaaS usually follow a tiered structure based on monthly uptime. A common pattern:

- 99.0% to 99.9% monthly uptime: 10% of the monthly fee
- 95.0% to 99.0%: 25%
- below 95.0%: 50%

A 3h40 outage in a 30-day month is about 99.49% uptime, so under that kind of table it would typically fall in the 10% tier.

Things to check before answering the customer:
1. Many contracts only count full unavailability as downtime. Delayed or stale data may not qualify.
2. Credits often have to be requested in writing within 30 days.
3. Credits are usually the customer's sole remedy and are applied to the next invoice, not paid in cash.

Your actual contract wording governs: look for the definitions of "Downtime", "Availability" and "Service Credit" in the MSA or SLA exhibit.
